title: Fast Start 14D Engineering Bootcamp + Interview Probe
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational playbook for a 14-day cross-functional engineering bootcamp that doubles as an interview probe for mid-senior IC hires (IC3–IC5). Goal: accelerate ramp, validate practical skills and team fit, and leave new hires (or candidates) with a clear 30/60/90 micro-plan.

Audience:
- Hiring managers running interview loops for mid-senior engineers
- People Ops and Talent Partners coordinating logistics
- Hiring committee members who need a consistent, fast evaluation framework

Success criteria (how we know it worked):
- Candidate/new hire completes 2 small shipped artifacts or merge-ready PRs during the 14d sprint, or produces a design doc + prototype.
- Hiring rubric median >= 3.5/5 across technical, collaboration, and autonomy axes for hires.
- New hire owner (manager) reports a clear 30-day plan and assigned mentor by Day 3.

High-level flow (14 days):
Day 0 (pre-bootcamp, coordinated by People Ops):
- Slack invite + team group, calendar blocks for core check-ins, access checklist (git, CI, docs, infra sandboxes).
- Assign mentor and onboarding buddy; share reading list and repo maps.

Day 1–2: Foundations + Context
- Orientation: company values quick intro (15m), team roadmap (30m), infra overview (45m).
- Small environment setup task (verify local dev, run tests, open a trivial PR).
- Manager 1:1 (expectations, immediate priorities)

Day 3–7: Problem pickup + interview probe
- Problem briefing: clear scoped ticket (bug/feature) + success criteria.
- Candidate works on ticket asynchronously; daily 15m standup with buddy.
- Checkpoint on Day 5: 30–45m design review with 2 reviewers (one from product or infra).
- Deliverable: PR draft or design doc and runnable demo.

Day 8–12: Integrate, test, and iterate
- Focus on code quality, tests, CI, deployment runbook.
- Pairing sessions (2x 60m) with a cross-functional engineer (infra/release/QA).
- Run performance/latency basic checks if relevant; summarise tradeoffs.

Day 13–14: Demo + retrospective + hiring decision
- Demo to team + cross-functional stakeholders (30m).
- Retro with candidate/new hire and mentor (30m).
- Hiring committee consolidation and rubric finalization.

Logistics checklist (People Ops):
- Pre-bootcamp: create calendar invitation with all sessions, add meeting owners, confirm reviewers for Day 5 and demo session.
- Environment access: ensure GitHub, internal CI, test cluster credentials available Day 0.
- Hardware: cloud credits or ephemeral sandbox provisioned.
- Communication: create private interview Slack channel for feedback; enable snippets for PR links.

Interview Rubric (single-page, 5-point scale) — purposefully lightweight for fast loops
- Technical execution (code quality, tests, debugging) — 1–5
- Design & tradeoffs (engineering judgment, architecture sense) — 1–5
- Deliverability & ownership (shipping mindset, follow-through) — 1–5
- Collaboration & communication (clarity in async + pairing) — 1–5
- Learning velocity & curiosity (asks good questions, accepts feedback) — 1–5

Scoring guidelines (anchor examples):
1 = misses core requirements, broken PR, no tests, poor communication
3 = meets requirements, code works, reasonable tests, has some tradeoff awareness
5 = polished, clear API/UX, strong tests, thoughtful tradeoff discussion, teaches reviewers

Pass/fail decision logic (for interview use):
- Median score >= 3.5 and no category <= 2 => recommend hire
- Median score 3.0–3.5 or any single category 2 => hold for calibration and additional pairing
- Median < 3.0 => decline

Manager & Mentor Checklist (first 14 days):
- Day 0: confirm mentor assigned and first-week calendar invites sent
- Day 1: 30-minute manager 1:1; share top 3 priorities; set expectations for bootcamp ticket
- Day 3: mentor check-in — environment green, PR started
- Day 5: attend design review; provide written feedback within 24h
- Day 7: confirm test/CI pass and shipping plan
- Day 10: review any performance considerations, prod-readiness gaps
- Day 14: hiring-retro + 30/60/90 draft; agree next steps

Artifact examples (pick 1–2 based on seniority):
- Mid IC: fix a flaky endpoint, add end-to-end tests, write a concise postmortem-style note on root cause
- Senior IC: design a small service component, deliver a diagram + proto + benchmark notes, open implementation PRs for core paths

Template prompts for design reviews and rubrics (copy/paste):
- "Context: What user need or reliability problem does this solve? What are constraints?"
- "Approach: What options did you evaluate? Why this one?"
- "Risks: What are the unknowns and rollback plan?"
- "Measurables: How will you know success (latency, error rate, cost)?"

Evaluation debrief flow (hiring loop):
1) Each reviewer submits rubric + short bullet feedback to private Slack channel within 24h.
2) Hiring manager collects rubric medians and writes a 3-sentence recommendation.
3) If ambiguous, schedule a 30m calibration call including an additional pairing session.

Quick tips & common pitfalls:
- Dont overload candidate with 1-week full rewrite tasks; keep scope small and observable.
- Prefer real infra tickets over synthetic puzzles; they reflect shipping behavior.
- Guard against bias: anonymize PR authorship in early reviews where possible.
- Use the bootcamp for two-way evaluation: candidate should also have clear signal about team cadence, codebase clarity, and autonomy levels.

Open questions / decisions to finalize (notes to self):
- Do we allow remote-only ephemeral infra or require access to staging clusters? (priority: low)
- Acceptance criteria for senior hires on benchmarking artifacts vs product prototypes.
- How many additional pairing sessions are acceptable before the loop stalls? Recommend max 2 ad-hoc pairing follow-ups.

Next steps (people-ops owners):
- Finalize playbook and circulate to hiring managers (owner: Aisha) — target: 2/28/2026
- Add a 1-question pulse survey for candidates about clarity and fairness of the bootcamp (owner: Marco)
- Create a single-page rubric card in Confluence and link to interview scheduling template (owner: Lena)

Revision history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft
- 2025-12-03: added scoring anchors and manager checklist
- 2026-02-20: updated logistics and finalized decision thresholds

Notes to reviewer:
This document is intentionally compact so hiring managers can run a fast, observable validation without heavy ops overhead. Feedback requested on: pass/fail thresholds, artifact examples for senior hires, and whether we should mandate anonymized PR reviews for the first design checkpoint.
